title: Module structures and functors transported by finite products
statement: Let C,D be small sites J,K and L:Sh(J,Set)⇄Sh(K,Set):V an adjunction with L preserving finite limits. Let R,S,A be sheaves of commutative rings, R on J and S,A on K. Suppose eR:|A|≅L|R| identifies the sectionwise addition and multiplication of R and A through the product comparison, and let c:A→S be a ring-sheaf map. On the module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], there exist functors I:Mod(R)→Mod(A) and P:Mod(S)→Mod(R), and natural isomorphisms eI:|I(-)|≅L|-| and eP:|P(-)|≅V|-|. For every M, its addition and scalar-action maps and those of I(M) have their ordinary sectionwise values, and their images under L agree through the binary-product comparison, eR and eI. For every H, its addition and scalar-action maps and those of P(H) have their ordinary sectionwise values. Addition is transported through V and eP. There is a map k:|R|×|P(H)|→V(|S|×|H|) whose projections are fst followed by the adjunct of eR⁻¹;c and snd followed by eP, and the scalar action of P(H) followed by eP equals k followed by V of the scalar action of H. No module hom-set equivalence or tensor adjunction is asserted.

source.place: Tags 03D1 and 03D2, lemma-pushforward-module and lemma-pullback-module; construction part of Tag 03D7

proof.text: The right adjoint V preserves finite limits, hence finite products. Transport the underlying additive group sheaves through L and V using internal commutative group objects and sectionwise reconstruction. Their addition diagrams are the respective product-comparison diagrams.

Transport the scalar action by the inverse product comparison. The two distributivity diagrams follow from product preservation and the given addition comparisons. The multiplicative associativity and unit diagrams follow in the same way; compatibility of eR with multiplication and its being invertible also identify the multiplicative unit. Evaluate these diagrams on sections to obtain the module laws.

Naturality of the action and the additive operations makes restriction maps semilinear. The underlying presheaf is already a set sheaf, so the section modules form a module sheaf. Apply the same formulas to a source linear map; its operation diagrams remain commutative, giving I on maps and its underlying natural isomorphism.

For V(H), restrict the transported VS action along the adjunct R→VS of eR⁻¹;c. This adjunct preserves ring operations by the product mate formula and the given ring comparison. V on linear maps gives P and eP. Define k by the inverse product comparison of V applied to the pair of this adjunct and eP. Its two projection equations follow from the product universal property; its scalar equation is the definition of the action.
